conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have three children - Alex, Blake, and Charlie. I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have three children - Alex, Blake, and Charlie. Let me ask you some questions about each of them to assess your eligibility.

Let's start with some general questions:

**How old are Alex, Blake, and Charlie?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 5 years old, Blake is 21, and Charlie is 13.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now let me ask about your relationship with each child:

**Do Alex, Blake, and Charlie all live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they all live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask about Blake specifically, since they are 21 years old:

**Is Blake currently in approved education or training?** (Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training, but normally stops at age 20.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are any of the children currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for extended periods?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Charlie was in care for a couple of months earlier, but that's finished now. Alex hasn't been in care or hospital, and neither has Blake.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I need to understand Charlie's situation a bit better:

**How long ago did Charlie leave care, and are they now living with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Charlie is back home with me now, living here full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just to clarify about Charlie's care situation:

**Is Charlie currently back living with you permanently, or is this a temporary arrangement? And when exactly did Charlie return home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Charlie is back home permanently now. They came back quite recently - it's only been a few weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are any of the children currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of them are working that much or receiving any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one final question:

**Are you currently claiming Child Benefit for any of these children, or has anyone else ever claimed Child Benefit for them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently claiming it for any of them, and nobody else has claimed it for them either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility

Based on the information you've provided, here's the assessment for each of your children:

### ✅ **Alex (age 5) - ELIGIBLE**
You can claim Child Benefit for Alex. As a 5-year-old child living with you in the UK, Alex meets all the eligibility criteria.

### ❌ **Blake (age 21) - INELIGIBLE**
Unfortunately, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Blake. Child Benefit normally covers children under 16, or can continue until age 20 if they're in approved education or training. Since Blake is 21 and not in education or training, they exceed the age limit for Child Benefit.

### ✅ **Charlie (age 13) - ELIGIBLE**
You can claim Child Benefit for Charlie. Although Charlie was in care earlier, they have now returned home permanently and are living with you full-time. Since Charlie is 13 years old and living with you, they meet the eligibility criteria.

## Next Steps

You can claim Child Benefit for **Alex and Charlie**. To make your claim, you can apply online or by post. 

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

Do you have any questions about your eligibility or the claims process?
